title: Proj of the tensor powers of an invertible ideal
statement:
If $\mathcal L$ is an invertible ideal on $Y$, the structure morphism

$$
\operatorname{Proj}_Y\Bigl(\bigoplus_{n\geq0}\mathcal L^n\Bigr)
\longrightarrow Y
$$

of the relative Proj of the Rees algebra of $\mathcal L$ is an
isomorphism.

proof.text: By the definition of invertibility and the affine-open basis, choose an affine cover $Y=\bigcup_i V_i$, $V_i=\operatorname{Spec}(A_i)$, on which $\mathcal L|_{V_i}$ has a basis $a_i$. Since $\mathcal L$ is an ideal subsheaf, multiplication by $a_i$ on $\mathcal O_{V_i}$ is injective: a section $r$ with $ra_i=0$ is zero by the basis isomorphism $\mathcal O_{V_i}\cong\mathcal L|_{V_i}$. Thus $a_i$ and all its powers are non-zero-divisors.

source.place: Tag 01IT, lemma-basis-affine-opens; blueprint proof, choice of affine trivializations

proof.text: Put $\mathcal R=\bigoplus_{n\geq0}\mathcal L^n$, with its sheaf Rees algebra structure. On $V_i$, the ideal-power subsheaf $\mathcal L^n$ is generated by $a_i^n$, and multiplication by $a_i^n$ identifies it with $\mathcal O_{V_i}$. The affine tilde--sections adjunction, its isomorphic unit and preservation of coproducts therefore identify $\mathcal R(V_i)$ with $\bigoplus_n A_i a_i^n$. Set $I_i=A_i a_i$ and $T_i=\bigoplus_n I_i^{\otimes_{A_i}n}$. In degree $n$, multiplication sends the basis $a_i^{\otimes n}$ to the basis $a_i^n$, so it is bijective (also for $n=0$). These maps form a graded $A_i$-algebra equivalence $T_i\cong\mathcal R(V_i)$: on basis multiples their products are $ra_i^m\cdot sa_i^n=rs a_i^{m+n}$, and degree zero is the identity.

source.place: Tags 01IB/01ID, lemma-equivalence-quasi-coherent and lemma-colimit-quasi-coherent; elementary basis calculation connecting the two versions of the affine node

proof.text: Let $\pi:P=\operatorname{Proj}_Y(\mathcal R)\to Y$. Relative-Proj existence identifies $\pi^{-1}(V_i)\to V_i$ with $\operatorname{Proj}(\mathcal R(V_i))\to V_i$. Apply graded-equivalence functoriality to the equivalence in step 2, which is the identity on the degree-zero base. The affine tensor-powers calculation identifies $\operatorname{Proj}(T_i)\to V_i$ with the identity of $V_i$. Consequently $\pi_i:\pi^{-1}(V_i)\to V_i$ is an isomorphism over $V_i$.

source.place: Whole proof, application of the affine calculation and relative-Proj restriction; Stacks 01NQ (lemma-glue-relative-proj) and 01MY/01N0 (graded equivalences)

proof.text: Write $s_i:V_i\to\pi^{-1}(V_i)$ for $\pi_i^{-1}$. On $W=V_i\cap V_j$, each $s_i$ restricts to $W\to\pi^{-1}(W)$, since $\pi s_i$ is the inclusion of $V_i$. Both restrictions are inverses of $\pi|_{\pi^{-1}(W)}$ and hence agree: if $s,t$ are such inverses then $s=s(\pi t)=(s\pi)t=t$. The scheme-morphism gluing lemma gives $s:Y\to P$. On each $V_i$, $\pi s$ is the identity; on each $\pi^{-1}(V_i)$, $s\pi$ is the identity. The uniqueness clause of the same gluing lemma, applied to these two open covers, gives $\pi s=1_Y$ and $s\pi=1_P$. Thus the specified structure morphism is an isomorphism. No intersection of affine opens is assumed affine.

source.place: Tag 01JB, lemma-glue, mapping property; explicit inverse gluing for the blueprint locality step

blueprint_update.statement:
If $\mathcal L$ is an invertible ideal on $Y$, the structure morphism

$$
\operatorname{Proj}_Y\Bigl(\bigoplus_{n\geq0}\mathcal L^n\Bigr)
\longrightarrow Y
$$

of the relative Proj of the Rees algebra of $\mathcal L$ is an
isomorphism.

proof.text:
Being an isomorphism is local on the target. Cover $Y$ by affine opens
$V=\operatorname{Spec}(A)$ on which $\mathcal L(V)=(a)$ for a
non-zero-divisor $a$. Over such a $V$ the relative Proj is
$\operatorname{Proj}(\bigoplus_{n\geq0}\mathcal L(V)^n)$ with its
structure morphism to $V$, which is an isomorphism by
[lemma-nagata-relative-proj-invertible-tensor-powers-affine]. Hence the
structure morphism is an isomorphism over every member of an open cover of
$Y$, and therefore an isomorphism.
